Note::NlpAccessor::diff_words¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::NlpAccessor::diff_words(const Note& other) const

Word-Level Difference Between Two Notes¶

diff_words(other) compares each cell of self against the matching cell of other one word at a time and returns only the changes as a TokenBatch of tag-prefixed tokens. It is the word-granularity member of the diff / align family — the change-only counterpart of align_tokens, and a sibling of diff_lines, diff_chars, and align_sentences.

How the comparison works¶

Each cell pair is tokenized into words by the same tokenizer as tokens: a word is a run of ASCII letters and digits, with _, an interior single -/', a trailing +/#, and recognized URLs / emails / dotted abbreviations kept whole. Spaces and standalone punctuation are dropped before the comparison — diff_words therefore never reports a punctuation-only edit; "stop here" and "stop, here!" diff to nothing.

The two word lists are aligned by their longest common subsequence, and only the differing words are emitted, in order, one per token, tagged in the first byte:

Tag

Meaning

In self

In other

-

removed — word in self, not matched in other

yes

no

+

added — word in other, not matched in self

no

yes

Words common to both sides produce no token, so a cell with no word-level change contributes an empty range. A substituted word appears as an adjacent -old / +new pair. For the full transcript that keeps the unchanged words as = tokens, use align_tokens — it runs the same alignment.

The TokenBatch result¶

Tokens from all cells are concatenated into the rank-1 Note batch.tokens(). The rank-1 Int64 Note batch.offsets() has length numel + 1 and marks each cell’s run: cell r owns tokens.at(k) for k in [offsets[r], offsets[r + 1]). Unchanged cells have offsets[r] == offsets[r + 1].

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

The comparison is per cell and pairwise. self and other must have the same numel, or one of them may be a scalar (numel() == 1) that is broadcast against every cell of the other; shape beyond the cell count is ignored, and offsets() follows the non-scalar side. Two rejections, both raising pluss::Error:

  • self in bytes mode → Note::NlpAccessor::diff_words requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes).

  • unequal numel with neither side a scalar → Note::NlpAccessor::diff_words expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

The alignment is O(m · n) in words per cell and fully deterministic: on a tie the walk emits the - (removal) before the + (insertion).

Example 1: Per-Cell Changes And Offsets¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::make_note({"the quick brown fox", "hello world"})
        .nlp().diff_words(pluss::make_note({"the slow brown fox", "hello there world"}));

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["-quick", "+slow", "+there"]
offsets: [0, 2, 3]

Cell 0’s edits are tokens()[0..2) — quick replaced by slow. Cell 1’s are tokens()[2..3) — there inserted between hello and world.

Example 2: Identical Cells Produce Nothing¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"no change here"})
                       .nlp().diff_words(pluss::make_note({"no change here"}));
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]
offsets: [0, 0]

Example 3: Scalar Broadcast On The Right¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"a b c", "a x c"})
                       .nlp().diff_words(pluss::make_note({"a b c"}));

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["-x", "+b"]
offsets: [0, 0, 2]

The single right-hand cell is compared against both left-hand cells. Cell 0 matches exactly (empty range); cell 1 differs by one word.

Example 4: Everything Inserted¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({""})
                       .nlp().diff_words(pluss::make_note({"brand new text"}));
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["+brand", "+new", "+text"]

An empty self cell has no words, so every word of other is a + token.

Example 5: Punctuation-Only Changes Are Ignored¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"stop here"})
                       .nlp().diff_words(pluss::make_note({"stop, here!"}));
std::cout << "token count: " << batch.tokens().numel() << "\n";

Output¶

token count: 0

The added comma and exclamation mark are separators, not words — no edit is reported.

Example 6: Rejections¶

try {
  (void)pluss::make_note({"a", "b"})
      .nlp().diff_words(pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c"}));
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

try {
  (void)pluss::note::bytes({"x"}).nlp().diff_words(pluss::make_note({"y"}));
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

Note::NlpAccessor::diff_words expects equal numel or scalar broadcast
Note::NlpAccessor::diff_words requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes)
